diagram_candidates.why: The algorithm traverses factorable expression DAGs and explicitly lifts a product node w=uv using four McCormick inequalities, with certified operand bounds and a convex outer enclosure. A bounded two-dimensional slice makes the graph and relaxation planes more immediate, while the procedure is fully specified in prose.
diagram_candidates.content_to_draw: Choose a concrete finite rectangle [l_x,u_x]×[l_y,u_y]. In 3D draw the bilinear graph w=xy over the rectangle and the four affine McCormick planes from def-mccormick-bilinear-box-envelope.md lines 30–33; show the vertical interval between the maximum lower plane and minimum upper plane as the relaxed fiber. Label this as a lifted convex hull/outer relaxation, not as the exact graph except at corners.

diagram_candidates.why: This worked example contrasts a unique global minimizer and the Cauchy step as distinct boundary points for one explicit indefinite quadratic, and computes their different predicted reductions. A small 2D figure could show this geometric comparison at a glance.
diagram_candidates.content_to_draw: Draw the unit disk for B=diag(-1,1), g=(-1,-3)/√2; mark p*=(1,1)/√2 and p_C=(1,3)/√10 on its boundary. Label the predicted reductions as 2 and √5−2/5 respectively. If contours are added, derive them from m(p)−f(x)=gᵀp+½pᵀBp and ensure their orientation matches the indefinite Hessian.

diagram_candidates.why: The example changes coordinates from two pixels to mean and half-difference, then states that the proximal map preserves the mean while soft-thresholding the half-difference. A simple graph can clarify the threshold action without adding mathematical claims.
diagram_candidates.content_to_draw: Plot d↦S_{tλ}(d)=sign(d)max(|d|−tλ,0), with threshold points ±tλ and zero plateau. Optionally pair it with v1,v2→(m,d)→(m−S_{tλ}(d),m+S_{tλ}(d)) to show that the mean coordinate stays fixed and only the difference shrinks.

diagram_candidates.why: The statement compares a centered chord and an unequal two-step stencil with the unit tangent of a smooth curve and gives second-order error bounds. A local curve sketch can orient the sample points and distinguish the symmetric and unequal stencils.
diagram_candidates.content_to_draw: Draw a unit-speed curve R(s) with tangent R′(s), centered sample points R(s−h), R(s+h), and their chord direction d_h; beside it show unequal sample offsets h_− and h_+ with the weighted stencil d_{h_−,h_+}. Mark that normalized directions are within 4δ_h or 4δ_{h_−,h_+} of R′(s); avoid implying the one-sided branch has a second-order bound.
